title: Persona and Tool-Call Pattern Notes
body:
Purpose and context:
- Quick working notes for a minimal, testable prompt architecture we can use when onboarding new chat-capable models into Redwood's serving runtime. Focus: clear persona boundaries + deterministic tool signals + lightweight safety scaffolds that let us detect regressions automatically.

Design goals (high level):
- Deterministic tool calling: make tool invocation explicit in model output so evaluator can parse reliably.
- Persona as constraint not narrative: short system/persona that constrains tone/verbosity but does not over-specify facts.
- Safety scaffolds: layered checks (pre-response, post-response verifier, fallback phrasing) to reduce unsafe outputs while preserving useful assistant behavior.
- Testability: every pattern should have 1+ unit evals (prompt-level regression checks) and 1+ integration evals (with mock tool stubs).

Constraints we care about for onboarding:
- Sequence length trimming: keep system + few-shot under 512 tokens for gpt-like models; prefer 3-shot max for heavy LLMs.
- Tool latency: tool calls should be referenced by short symbolic tags to avoid long model-generated payloads.
- Model variability: design prompts that surface disagreements between base model and quantized variants.

Core prompt primitives (suggested templates)
1) System (single short string)
- "You are a concise, user-focused assistant for developer workflows. Prioritize accuracy, cite sources when available, and use tool calls (MARKER_CALL) when a query requires external data or state. If you detect sensitive content or safety violations, stop and return the tag [SENSITIVE]."

2) Persona (optional developer-facing note)
- "Tone: pragmatic, low-verbosity. Assume technical background unless user says otherwise. When uncertain, ask one clarifying question rather than guessing."

3) Tool-call syntactic convention
- Use a clear machine-parseable wrapper so runtime can detect calls without relying on heuristics. Example: <TOOL name=weather service_id=1>args: {"city":"Seattle","date":"2026-02-20"}</TOOL>
- Simpler alternative for early tests: [[TOOL:weather|city=Seattle|date=2026-02-20]]
- Important: models should place tool call at the end of an assistant message when invoking, and include a short human-facing line before the wrapper, e.g., "I can check that for you. Invoking tool now.\n<TOOL ...>"

4) Tool result consumption pattern
- When the tool returns, prompt scaffold should instruct the assistant to: 1) summarize salient fields, 2) cite the tool name and timestamp, 3) label uncertainty. Example post-tool: "Tool result (weather): 55°F, rain. Source: weather-v1@2026-02-20. Confidence: high. Interpretation: bring umbrella."

Safety scaffolds (layered):
A) Pre-response guard: system message contains a short checklist instructing the model to not hallucinate personal data or protected categories. If unsafe, respond exactly with [SENSITIVE].
B) Post-generation verifier: a small deterministic rubric-runner (in evaluator harness) checks outputs for PII, hate, and medical/legal claims; if flagged -> mark as regression and require manual review.
C) Fallback phrasing: instruct model to use safe fallback templates when unsure. Examples: "I don't have enough information to answer that safely; can you provide more context?" or return structured token [NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW].

Sample prompt flow for an onboarding test case:
- User: "Summarize the last 3 commits to repo X and run tests."
- System: (as above)
- Assistant (expected behavior): 1) Recognize need for tools (repo-list, test-run). 2) Emit: "I will fetch commits and run tests. Invoking tools now.\n[[TOOL:git-commits|repo=X|n=3]]\n[[TOOL:ci-run|repo=X|matrix=unit]]"
- Mock tool returns: commits list, ci result OK/FAIL.
- Assistant final: human-facing summary + structured result block: {"commits":[...],"tests":"PASS","actions":"none"}
- Evaluation checks: did assistant call both tools in correct syntax? Did assistant summarize tool output and not fabricate additional commit messages?

Regression signal design:
- Unit-level signals (fast): parseable counts (tool invocations present? yes/no), presence of tags [SENSITIVE],[NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW], character length, presence of verbatim tool wrappers.
- Semantic-level signals (slower): embedding-based similarity of response to golden answers, hallucination score computed by cross-checking returned facts against tool outputs.
- Thresholds: major regression if tool-call omission increases >5% across a promptset; or hallucination-score rises by 10% relative to baseline.

Promptset construction guidelines
- Balance of intents: 40% tool-heavy (requires 1+ tools), 30% short-answer, 20% conversational follow-ups, 10% adversarial/safety probes.
- For each prompt, provide: a) short spec, b) gold parseable tool sequence (if any), c) expected summary fields, d) tags for tests (safety, privacy, numeric reasoning).
- Use slot-ized variables for scale testing e.g., {{repo}}, {{city}}, {{date}}. Create 5 variants per slot to surface brittleness.

Evaluation harness notes
- Runner should: 1) inject system+persona, 2) replay user message, 3) intercept assistant messages and assert wrapper formats, 4) feed mock tool responses, 5) collect final assistant output and run rubrics.
- Include a lightweight parser that tolerates whitespace/noise (regex-based) and a strict parser mode for gating release.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Exact verbosity cap for system/persona combined. Too short -> model ignores constraint. Too long -> eats token budget. Proposed compromise: system <= 60 tokens, persona <= 25 tokens. Need empirical check across 3 models.
- How to best surface tool errors to the user while keeping structured signals clear? Current idea: always emit a machine-readable error block and a one-sentence human explanation.
- Where to host the canonical wrapper spec? Confluence vs JSON schema in repo. Prefer JSON schema + short confluence doc that maps to runtime.

Short checklist before an onboarding PR:
- [ ] Prompt templates added to prompt-harness repo under new folder (persona-tool-patterns).
- [ ] 20 prompt variants created (see promptset construction guidelines).
- [ ] Unit evals for wrapper detection implemented.
- [ ] Safety rubric integration wired into CI.
- [ ] Linked JIRA created for model-specific tuning if failures > 10% on unit signals.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally terse and iterative. Expect follow-ups: concrete JSON schemas for wrappers, an ADR for the fallback tags, and a small experiment matrix (3 models x 2 quant levels x 4 prompt variants) to validate thresholds.

Quick example entries for prompt-harness CSV (columns):
- prompt_id, intent, user_text, expected_tools, expected_summary_keys, tags
- e.g., P-001, repo-summary, "Summarize repo {{repo}} last 3 commits and run unit tests.", "git-commits,ci-run", "commits,tests,actions", "tool-heavy,code,regression"

End of notes.
